timeline.title: FISCAL TIMELINE
timeline.ir1914: Income tax created. Top rate: 2%. A 'temporary' wartime measure.
timeline.tip1928: TIP created (ancestor of modern fuel excise duty).
timeline.secu1945: Social Security created. Social contributions begin.
timeline.tva1954: VAT invented by Maurice Lauré. Initial rate: 16.85%.
timeline.csg1991: CSG created. Presented as 'temporary'. Initial rate: 1.1%.
timeline.crds1996: CRDS created to repay social debt. Still active 30 years later.
timeline.tmi2012: Top rate raised to 45%. 75% 'supertax' attempted (>€1M), struck down.
timeline.pfu2018: Flat Tax (PFU) created at 30%. Wealth tax (ISF) replaced by IFI.
timeline.carbon2019: Carbon tax frozen at €44.60/ton after the Yellow Vests movement.
timeline.csg2025: CSG: still at 9.2%. CRDS: still at 0.5%.
timeline.cdhr2026: CDHR: minimum 20% effective tax rate. CSG raised to 10.6% on investment income. Flat Tax: 31.4%.

footer.disclaimer: Data from official sources (OECD, INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP, Loi de finances). Satirical presentation.

detailIncomeTax.metaDescription: France's progressive income tax brackets 2026 (2025 income). 5 escalation stages, from 0% to 45%. Official data, satirical framing.
detailIncomeTax.title: INCOME TAX
detailIncomeTax.subtitle: FISCAL ESCALATION REPORT — 2026 Brackets (2025 income)
detailIncomeTax.intro: The French income tax is a progressive tax with brackets. Each bracket is another escalation level in state extraction. The schedule is indexed to inflation (+0.9% in 2026), meaning the State politely adjusts the starting point before extracting exactly as much as before.
detailIncomeTax.quotientDesc: The family quotient divides taxable income by the number of household shares. It's the only mechanism that acknowledges children eat.
detailIncomeTax.cdhrDesc: The Differential Contribution on High Incomes (CDHR) guarantees a minimum 20% effective tax rate for the wealthiest households. For those who thought tax optimization was a national sport, the State just changed the rules mid-game.

detailCorporateTax.metaDescription: French corporate tax rates: 25% standard, 15% SME. Exceptional surcharge for large companies. Official data.
detailCorporateTax.title: CORPORATE TAX
detailCorporateTax.subtitle: CORPORATE EXTRACTION REPORT — Rates 2025-2026
detailCorporateTax.intro: The corporate income tax (IS) is the tribute French companies pay to the State for the privilege of existing on national territory. With a standard rate of 25%, France maintains itself in the upper-middle European range — a ranking it defends with the same tenacity as its #1 global position in overall tax pressure.
detailCorporateTax.normalRateDesc: The standard rate applicable to all companies, without exception, without mercy.
detailCorporateTax.pmeRateDesc: A 15% rate on the first €42,500 of profit, reserved for SMEs meeting all conditions. Beyond that, back to the standard rate.
detailCorporateTax.pmeThreshold: Applies to the first €42,500 of profit only
detailCorporateTax.socialContributionDesc: A 3.3% surcharge for companies with revenue exceeding €7.63M and IS exceeding €763,000. Because one corporate tax wasn't enough.
detailCorporateTax.exceptionalDesc: For large companies, an 'exceptional' (but renewed) contribution:
detailCorporateTax.exceptionalNote: Source: Loi de finances 2025, extended to 2026.
detailCorporateTax.pendingDesc: The 2026 budget bill planned to raise the reduced rate threshold from €42,500 to €100,000, but this has not yet been enacted.

detailFlatTax.metaTitle: Flat Tax / PFU — Flat-Rate Withholding | impots.tax
detailFlatTax.metaDescription: Flat Tax 30% in 2025, 31.4% in 2026. Dividends, interest, capital gains, crypto. CSG increase from 9.2% to 10.6%.
detailFlatTax.title: FLAT TAX / PFU
detailFlatTax.subtitle: FLAT-RATE WITHHOLDING TAX REPORT
detailFlatTax.intro: The Prélèvement Forfaitaire Unique (PFU), known as the 'Flat Tax', was created in 2018 to simplify capital taxation. One rate, one operation. It was beautiful. It was simple. Which is why the State decided to complicate it in 2026 by increasing the CSG on investment income.
detailFlatTax.changeDesc: The CSG on capital income rises from 9.2% to 10.6%, bringing total social levies from 17.2% to 18.6%. The 'Flat Tax' isn't so flat anymore.
detailFlatTax.scopeCapitalGains: Capital gains on securities (stocks, bonds, funds)
detailFlatTax.scopeCrypto: Crypto capital gains (upon conversion to euros, exemption threshold: €305/year in disposals)
detailFlatTax.exceptionDesc: Some products retain the old 17.2% social levies: life insurance, PEL/CEL savings, PEP. Total PFU: 30%.
detailFlatTax.optionDesc: You can choose the progressive scale instead of the Flat Tax each year (box 2OP on the tax return). This choice is global and irrevocable for the year. Advantageous if your marginal rate is ≤ 11%. For dividends, a 40% allowance applies only with the progressive scale.

detailVat.metaDescription: France's 4 VAT rates: 20%, 10%, 5.5%, 2.1%. Invented in France in 1954. The most discreet and efficient tax ever created.
detailVat.title: VAT
detailVat.subtitle: REPORT ON THE MOST EFFICIENT FISCAL WEAPON EVER INVENTED
detailVat.intro: The Value Added Tax is France's most exported fiscal invention. Created in 1954 by Maurice Lauré, it is now used by over 170 countries. Its genius: it's invisible. You pay it with every purchase without ever seeing it. The perfect tax according to the State — the one you don't notice.
detailVat.rateNormalDesc: The majority of goods and services. Electronics, clothing, professional services, alcohol… everything that doesn't qualify for an exception.
detailVat.rateIntermediateDesc: Restaurants, passenger transport, energy renovation work, non-reimbursed medication, camping, museums.
detailVat.rateReducedDesc: Food (except alcohol, confectionery, caviar), books, energy (gas, electricity), equipment for disabled persons, live performances.
detailVat.rateSuperReducedDesc: Print and online press, medications reimbursed by Social Security, TV license fee (public broadcasting contribution).
detailVat.historyDesc: VAT was invented in France in 1954 by Maurice Lauré, a finance inspector. The initial rate was 16.85%. Today, the standard rate is 20%. The State decided 16.85% wasn't round enough — or profitable enough.
detailVat.mechanismDesc: VAT is collected at every stage of the production and distribution chain. Each business only remits VAT on its value added (collected VAT - deductible VAT). The final consumer bears the entire tax. It's a consumption tax, not a production tax.

detailFuelTax.metaTitle: Fuel Taxes — Excise Duty, TICPE, VAT | impots.tax
detailFuelTax.metaDescription: 55% of gasoline price is taxes. Excise duty, VAT on excise (tax on tax). Complete SP95 price breakdown.
detailFuelTax.title: FUEL TAXES
detailFuelTax.subtitle: EXTRACTION COST ANALYSIS — SP95 Unleaded, February 2026
detailFuelTax.intro: When you fill up your tank, you think you're buying gasoline. In reality, you're mostly funding the State. Out of every liter of SP95 at €1.71, about €0.95 goes to taxes. And the best part: VAT is applied ON TOP of the excise duty. Yes, it's a tax on a tax. France invented VAT, and it stops at nothing to apply it.
detailFuelTax.taxOnTaxDesc: The 20% VAT applies to the pre-VAT price, which includes the excise duty. Concretely, you pay VAT on the excise duty: ~€0.13 per liter of tax on a tax. It's perfectly legal, perfectly absurd, and perfectly French.
detailFuelTax.carbonDesc: The carbon tax has been frozen at €44.60 per ton of CO2 since 2018, following the Yellow Vests movement. It was supposed to reach €100/ton by 2030. The government preferred to avoid another episode of roundabout democracy.
detailFuelTax.sourceText: UFIP Énergies & Mobilités, Fipeco, Connaissance des Énergies, CNEWS (February-March 2026 data)

detailBehavioralTax.metaTitle: Behavioral Taxes — Tobacco, Alcohol, Sugar | impots.tax
detailBehavioralTax.metaDescription: 82% of a cigarette pack price is taxes. From €1.50 in 1990 to €13 in 2025. Complete breakdown.
detailBehavioralTax.title: BEHAVIORAL TAXES
detailBehavioralTax.subtitle: VICE FISCAL CONTROL REPORT — 2025-2026
detailBehavioralTax.intro: Behavioral taxes are the moralizing branch of the tax system. The State taxes what it disapproves of — tobacco, alcohol, sugar — while handsomely profiting from the revenue. The paradox: if everyone quit smoking tomorrow, the State budget would have a €14 billion hole.
detailBehavioralTax.tobaccoPMP: Weighted average price 2025: €12.54 per pack of 20 cigarettes
detailBehavioralTax.acciseSpecific: Specific component: €68.10 per 1,000 units (€3.405 per pack of 20)
detailBehavioralTax.evolutionDesc: The price of a pack went from ~€1.50 in 1990 to ~€13 in 2025, a +766% increase in 35 years. Inflation over the same period: ~80%. The difference is fiscal strategy.
detailBehavioralTax.alcoholDesc: Data being compiled. Excise duties on spirits, wine, and beer will be updated soon.
detailBehavioralTax.sugarDesc: Data being compiled. The contribution on sweetened beverages will be documented shortly.
detailBehavioralTax.sourceText: French Customs, Revue des Tabacs, Smoking.fr

detailSalaryContributions.metaTitle: Salary & Social Contributions — The True Cost of Labor | impots.tax
detailSalaryContributions.metaDescription: ~52% total social contributions. Complete employer/employee breakdown: health, pension, unemployment, CSG, CRDS. The journey of €100.
detailSalaryContributions.title: SALARY & CONTRIBUTIONS
detailSalaryContributions.subtitle: FIELD DAMAGE ASSESSMENT — Private Sector, 2025
detailSalaryContributions.intro: The French payslip is a masterpiece of administrative complexity. Between the total employer cost and what arrives in your bank account, the State and its agencies extract about 52% in various contributions. Welcome to the damage assessment report.
detailSalaryContributions.note1: Health: rises to 13% employer above 2.5× minimum wage
detailSalaryContributions.note2: Family allowances: rise to 5.25% above 3.5× minimum wage
detailSalaryContributions.note5: Transport levy: varies by municipality, 0 to ~3%
detailSalaryContributions.journeySubtitle: Estimate based on median net salary ~€2,400/month, 30% marginal rate
detailSalaryContributions.sourceText: URSSAF schedule 2025, CAPEB table 2025, Cleiss.fr, CCI

detailWelfareSystem.metaTitle: French Welfare System — RSA, AAH, ARE, AME | impots.tax
detailWelfareSystem.metaDescription: RSA €646/month, AAH €1,033/month, ARE ~57% of salary, AME €1.386B. Conditions, amounts, beneficiaries. Official data.
detailWelfareSystem.title: WELFARE SYSTEM
detailWelfareSystem.subtitle: NATIONAL SAFETY NET REPORT — 2025
detailWelfareSystem.intro: The French welfare system is one of the most generous in the world. It is also one of the most expensive. Here is the detail of four major programs: RSA, AAH, ARE, and AME. Every euro collected through social contributions funds — among other things — these benefits.
detailWelfareSystem.rsaDesc: The RSA is the guaranteed minimum income for people with no or very low income. Created in 2009 to replace the RMI, it is the last safety net of the French social system.
detailWelfareSystem.rsaNonTakeUpNote: About one-third of eligible people do not claim the RSA.
detailWelfareSystem.aahDesc: The AAH is a financial aid for people with disabilities who cannot — or can barely — work.
detailWelfareSystem.aahCondition2: Or disability rate 50-79% with substantial restriction on access to employment
detailWelfareSystem.aahDeconjugalization: Deconjugalization: effective since October 2023. Spouse's income is no longer taken into account.
detailWelfareSystem.areDesc: The ARE is unemployment insurance paid by France Travail to job seekers who have contributed sufficiently.
detailWelfareSystem.areCondition1: Must have worked at least 6 months (130 days or 910 hours)
detailWelfareSystem.areCondition2: Within the last 24 months (36 months for those ≥ 53)
detailWelfareSystem.areDuration: Variable, up to 24 months (36 months for those ≥ 55)
detailWelfareSystem.areCalcDesc: About 57% of daily reference wage (or 40.4% + €12.95/day, whichever is higher).
detailWelfareSystem.areFunding: Funding: employer contribution (4% of gross since May 2025)
detailWelfareSystem.ameDesc: The AME provides healthcare access to undocumented immigrants in France. Created in 2000, it is a recurring subject of debate.
detailWelfareSystem.ameCondition1: Resident in France for over 3 months
detailWelfareSystem.ameBudget: 2024 budget: €1.386B (actual spending), allocated budget frozen at €1.2B
detailWelfareSystem.ameCoverage: Coverage: 100% of Social Security rates, no extra charges
detailWelfareSystem.sourceText: aide-sociale.fr, Service-Public.fr, monparcourshandicap.gouv.fr, handicap.fr, France Travail, Senate (Delahaye report), Boursorama, LDH, OID

detailComparison.metaTitle: International Comparison — Tax-to-GDP OECD Ranking | impots.tax
detailComparison.metaDescription: France #1 worldwide with 46.1% tax-to-GDP. +12.6 points above OECD average. Full ranking of 14 countries.
detailComparison.title: INTERNATIONAL COMPARISON
detailComparison.subtitle: INTELLIGENCE REPORT — OECD Extraction Rate Rankings
detailComparison.intro: France holds the #1 global position in tax pressure according to the OECD, with a tax-to-GDP ratio of 46.1%. That's 12.6 points above the OECD average (33.5%). For perspective: France extracts proportionally more than Sweden (41.3%), a country synonymous with a massive welfare state. The French extraction rate even exceeds historical estimates of the Soviet peak.
detailComparison.analysisP1: France collects 46.1% of its GDP in taxes and contributions, placing it ahead of Denmark (43.4%) and Belgium (42.9%). The gap with the United States (27.7%) is 18.4 points — nearly double.
detailComparison.analysisP2: Switzerland, a neighboring country, collects only 27.6% of its GDP. A French person crossing the border literally enters a different fiscal world.
detailComparison.analysisP3: Mexico (17.7%) shows it's possible to run a state with less than 20% in levies. The results are… different.

detailIndicators.metaTitle: Macro Indicators — Debt, Deficit, Public Spending | impots.tax
detailIndicators.metaDescription: Public debt €3,228B (112% of GDP), spending 56.5% of GDP, deficit -5.4%. The numbers that sum up the situation.
detailIndicators.title: MACRO INDICATORS
detailIndicators.subtitle: GENERAL SITUATION REPORT — France, 2024-2025
detailIndicators.intro: Here are the numbers that sum up France's financial situation. A debt exceeding €3,200 billion, public spending among the highest in the world, and a deficit that won't close. These indicators are the result of decades of fiscal policy — the very policy this dashboard documents.
detailIndicators.debtNote: For every euro of wealth produced in France, the State owes €1.12 to its creditors.
detailIndicators.spendingNote: Among the highest ratios in the OECD. More than half of national wealth passes through State coffers.
detailIndicators.deficitNote: Despite record tax pressure (46.1% of GDP), the State still spends more than it collects. The deficit is the gap between what the State takes and what it spends — and it spends more.
detailIndicators.summaryDesc: France is the country that collects the most taxes in the world (46.1% of GDP), spends the most (~56.5% of GDP), and despite all that, keeps accumulating more debt (112% of GDP). The equation only works thanks to borrowing capacity — as long as markets keep lending.
